title: The Ozone Layer
text: The ozone layer is a region of Earth's stratosphere, approximately 15 to 35 km above the surface, containing high concentrations of ozone (O3) that absorbs the majority of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation. The discovery of an ozone hole over Antarctica by British researchers in 1985 led to international concern. The Montreal Protocol, adopted in 1987, successfully phased out chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and other ozone-depleting substances. As a result, the ozone layer is slowly recovering and is expected to return to 1980 levels by mid-century. The ozone layer protects life on Earth from harmful UV-B and UV-C radiation, which can cause skin cancer, cataracts, and damage to marine ecosystems.
